arxiv-2105-10590.title: Parallelizing Contextual Bandits
arxiv-2105-10590.creator: Jeffrey Chan, Aldo Pacchiano, Nilesh Tripuraneni, Yun S. Song, Peter Bartlett, Michael I. Jordan
arxiv-2105-10590.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jeffrey Chan, Aldo Pacchiano, Nilesh Tripuraneni, Yun S. Song, Peter Bartlett, Michael I. Jordan. Standard approaches to decision-making under uncertainty focus on sequential exploration of the space of decisions. However, simultaneously proposing a batch of decisions, which leverages available resources for parallel experimentation, has the potential to rapidly accelerate exploration.

arxiv-2109-12457.title: Learning to Selectively Learn for Weakly-supervised Paraphrase Generation
arxiv-2109-12457.creator: Kaize Ding, Dingcheng Li, Alexander Hanbo Li, Xing Fan, Chenlei Guo, Yang Liu, Huan Liu
arxiv-2109-12457.description: Abstract Paraphrase generation is a longstanding NLP task that has diverse applications for downstream NLP tasks. However, the effectiveness of existing efforts predominantly relies on large amounts of golden labeled data. Though unsupervised endeavors have been proposed to address this issue, they may fail to generate meaningful paraphrases due to the lack of supervision signals.

This problem is more pronounced on zero-shot translation tasks. arxiv-2405-04662.title: Radar Fields: Frequency-Space Neural Scene Representations for FMCW Radar
arxiv-2405-04662.creator: David Borts, Erich Liang, Tim Brödermann, Andrea Ramazzina, Stefanie Walz, Edoardo Palladin, Jipeng Sun, David Bruggemann, Christos Sakaridis, Luc Van Gool, Mario Bijelic, Felix Heide
arxiv-2405-04662.description: Abstract . Neural fields have been broadly investigated as scene representations for the reproduction and novel generation of diverse outdoor scenes, including those autonomous vehicles and robots must handle. While successful approaches for RGB and LiDAR data exist, neural reconstruction methods for radar as a sensing modality have been largely unexplored.

arxiv-2407-09663.title: Rotation in the Geometric Scalar Theory of Gravity
arxiv-2407-09663.creator: and Vicente Antunes
arxiv-2407-09663.description: Abstract We present solutions corresponding to rotational configurations in the recently proposed Geometric Scalar Gravity (GSG) theory. The solutions obtained here have the important property that the associated closed time-like curves are always restricted to a compact domain of space-time. We compare this property with those of analogous solutions in General Relativity (GR).

arxiv-2408-01592.title: OGLE-IV Period-Luminosity relation of the LMC: an analysis using mean and median magnitudes
arxiv-2408-01592.creator: Jaime Muñoz, Alejandro García-Varela, Santiago Henao-Castellanos, Beatriz Sabogal, Luis Felipe Giraldo, Jorge Martínez † \dagger
arxiv-2408-01592.description: Abstract The Period-Luminosity (PL) relation for Cepheid variable stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) is crucial for distance measurements in astronomy. This study analyzes the impact of using the median rather than the mean on the PL relation’s slope and zero point.

arxiv-2411-14545.title: Non-Hermitian Spin-Spin Interaction Mediated by Chiral Phonons
arxiv-2411-14545.creator: Haowei Xu, Guoqing Wang, Changhao Li, Hao Tang, Paola Cappellaro, Ju Li
arxiv-2411-14545.description: Abstract Non-Hermiticity and chirality are two fundamental properties known to give rise to various intriguing phenomena. However, the interplay between these properties has been rarely explored. In this work, we bridge this gap by introducing an off-diagonal non-Hermitian spin-spin interaction mediated by chiral phonons.

arxiv-2506-02345.creator: Alex Broihier, Stefanos Baziotis, Daniel Kang, Charith Mendis
arxiv-2506-02345.description: Abstract . The Pandas API has been central to the success of pandas and its alternatives. Despite its importance, there is no benchmark for it, and we argue that we cannot repurpose existing benchmarks (from other domains) for the Pandas API.

britannica-1911-shrike.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-shrike.description: Article 'Shrike' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 24), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The species designated shrike by Turner is the Lanius excubitor of Linnaeus and nearly all succeeding authors, nowadays commonly known as the greater butcher-bird, ash-coloured or great grey shrike—a bird which visits the British Islands pretty regularly, though not numerously, in autumn or winter, occasionally prolonging its stay into the next summer; but it has never been ascertained to breed there, though often asserted to have done so.

pmc-10520415.title: Use of baclofen and propranolol for treatment of neurogenic fever in a patient with pontine hemorrhage: A case report
pmc-10520415.creator: Saroj Poudel, Rupak Chalise, Manoj Bist, Ashim Regmi, Anup Ghimire, Kishor Khanal
pmc-10520415.description: Key Clinical MessageNeurogenic fever (NF) is a potentially life‐threatening complication commonly seen in patients with pontine hemorrhage. This case report highlights the successful use of oral baclofen and propranolol as an effective treatment strategy to manage NF.AbstractNeurogenic fever (NF) is a common complication following pontine hemorrhage and poses significant challenges for clinicians in terms of diagnosis, management, and patient outcomes.

pmc-12436875.title: Repurposing Oxytocin as A New Predictor for Metabolic Syndrome in Schizophrenia
pmc-12436875.creator: K. K. Goh, M. L. Lu
pmc-12436875.description: IntroductionThe increasing prevalence of metabolic syndrome in persons with schizophrenia has driven research into the underlying mechanisms of its pathophysiology. Overlapping neurobiological profiles of metabolic risk factors and psychiatric symptoms, particularly shared genetic liabilities, suggest that oxytocin system dysfunction may be a common mechanism underlying both schizophrenia and metabolic syndrome.

pmc-12672352.title: The impact of frailty on cognitive outcomes in elderly patients with post-stroke subjective cognitive complaints
pmc-12672352.creator: Jiayu Duan, Yunling Zhang, Xianglan Jin, Shaozhen Ji
pmc-12672352.description: Background and purposeFrailty delineates a state of poor health characterized by the accumulation of age-related health deficits, and was associated with cognitive decline in patients with subjective cognitive complaints (SCC). However, whether cognitive recovery is related to frailty in elderly patients with post-stroke SCC remained unknown.
